title: A.3 Work, Energy and Power
subject: IBDP Physics
introduction: Energy is one of the most important concepts in physics. It describes the ability of a system to cause change or perform work. Energy can be transferred between objects or transformed from one form into another, but the total amount of energy in a closed system remains constant. Understanding work, energy and power allows physicists to analyse motion, machines, electrical systems and natural processes.
learning_objectives: Explain energy transfer and energy transformation.
Calculate work done by a force.

definitions.meaning: The ability of a system to do work or cause change. Energy is measured in joules (J).
The transfer of energy when a force causes an object to move through a distance.
The rate at which energy is transferred or work is done.
The energy possessed by an object due to its motion.
Energy stored in an object because of its position in a gravitational field.
The ratio of useful energy output to total energy input.

core_concepts.heading: Energy Transfer
core_concepts.explanation: Energy can move from one object to another or change from one form to another. Examples include chemical energy changing into kinetic energy in a moving car, or electrical energy changing into light energy in a lamp.

core_concepts.heading: Conservation of Energy
core_concepts.explanation: Energy cannot be created or destroyed. It can only be transferred or transformed between different forms. The total energy in a closed system remains constant.

core_concepts.heading: Work Done
core_concepts.explanation: Work is done when a force causes displacement in the direction of the force. A larger force or larger displacement results in more energy transfer.

core_concepts.heading: Power
core_concepts.explanation: Power measures how quickly energy is transferred. Two machines can do the same amount of work, but the machine that completes the task faster has greater power.

energy_types.name: Kinetic Energy
energy_types.explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy an object has because of its motion. It depends on both the mass of the object and its velocity.

energy_types.name: Gravitational Potential Energy
energy_types.explanation: Gravitational potential energy is stored energy due to an object's position in a gravitational field. Increasing height increases the stored energy.

energy_types.name: Elastic Potential Energy
energy_types.explanation: Elastic potential energy is stored when an elastic object such as a spring is stretched or compressed.

energy_types.name: Thermal Energy
energy_types.explanation: Thermal energy is related to the random movement of particles inside a substance. Heating increases the internal energy of a system.

energy_types.name: Chemical Energy
energy_types.explanation: Chemical energy is stored in chemical bonds and can be released during chemical reactions.

formulas.name: Work Done

variables.s: distance moved in direction of force (m)

formulas.explanation: Work done represents energy transferred when a force moves an object through a distance.

formulas.name: Kinetic Energy
formulas.explanation: Kinetic energy increases with the square of velocity, meaning small increases in velocity create larger energy changes.

formulas.name: Gravitational Potential Energy
formulas.explanation: Objects gain gravitational potential energy when raised in a gravitational field.

formulas.name: Power
formulas.explanation: Power measures how quickly energy is transferred.

formulas.name: Efficiency
formulas.formula: Efficiency = useful output energy / total input energy × 100
formulas.explanation: Efficiency shows how much input energy becomes useful output energy.

worked_examples.question: A 2 kg object moves at 10 m/s. Calculate its kinetic energy.
A 5 kg object is lifted 4 m. Calculate gravitational potential energy.

energy_conservation.explanation: The conservation of energy principle states that energy cannot be created or destroyed. It can only be transferred between objects or transformed from one form to another. In a closed system, the total energy before and after a process remains constant.
energy_conservation.example: When a ball falls from a height, gravitational potential energy decreases while kinetic energy increases. The total energy remains constant if air resistance is ignored.

energy_conservation.explanation: Energy can be transferred through mechanical work, electrical work, heating and radiation. Understanding transfer pathways helps analyse complex systems.
examples: A motor transfers electrical energy into kinetic energy.
A heater transfers electrical energy into thermal energy.
A battery transfers chemical energy into electrical energy.

energy_diagrams.explanation: A Sankey diagram represents energy transfers in a system. The width of each arrow represents the amount of energy transferred.
Energy flow diagrams show the input energy, useful output energy and wasted energy in a system.

efficiency_examples.question: A machine receives 500 J of energy and produces 400 J of useful energy. Calculate efficiency.
solution: Efficiency = useful output energy / total input energy × 100

efficiency_examples.question: A motor transfers 2000 J of electrical energy and produces 1200 J of kinetic energy. Find wasted energy.
solution: Wasted energy = input energy - useful output energy

common_mistakes: Confusing energy with power. Energy is the amount transferred, while power is the rate of transfer.
Forgetting to convert units before calculations.
Using mass in grams instead of kilograms.
Using velocity instead of speed in kinetic energy calculations.
Ignoring the square on velocity in kinetic energy equations.
Not identifying useful and wasted energy correctly.
ib_exam_tips: Always state the energy transfer pathway.
Draw energy diagrams when explaining transformations.
Use conservation of energy when analysing systems.

hl_extension.explanation: The work done on an object is equal to its change in kinetic energy. This connects forces and energy.
Mechanical power depends on the force applied and the velocity of movement.
Objects moving in circular paths continuously exchange energy between different forms depending on the system.

real_world_applications: Car manufacturers analyse energy efficiency to reduce fuel consumption.
Renewable energy systems convert natural energy sources into electrical energy.
Engineers calculate power requirements for machines.
Buildings use energy analysis to reduce heat losses.

practice_questions.question: A machine uses 1000 J of energy and gives 700 J useful output. Calculate efficiency.
A 3 kg object moves at 8 m/s. Calculate its kinetic energy.
Explain how increasing velocity affects kinetic energy.
practice_questions.answer: Kinetic energy increases with the square of velocity, so doubling velocity increases kinetic energy by four times.

summary: Work, energy and power provide a method to analyse how energy moves and changes in physical systems. By applying conservation of energy, students can understand mechanical systems, calculate energy transfers and evaluate efficiency. These concepts are used throughout physics, engineering and technology.
